title: The symptom spectrum: preoperative symptom-related indicators of surgical outcomes for adult type 1 chiari malformation
The 2026 Canadian Undergraduate Medical Physics Conference Abstract Book
journal: Undergraduate Research in Natural and Clinical Science and Technology Journal
abstract: The Canadian Undergraduate Medical Physics Conference (CUMPC) is a national, two-day conference that brings together undergraduate students from across Canada who are conducting medical physics research or are interested in exploring the field. CUMPC provides a virtual platform for students to showcase their medical physics research. Students are invited to submit research abstracts, which are externally reviewed and returned with constructive feedback. Selected participants are then invited to present their work, which is evaluated by a panel of experts. Awards are presented to the top three oral presentations in each category. This year’s theme, From Student to Professional: Navigating Career Pathways in Medical Physics, focuses on helping students explore the diverse career opportunities available in the field. The conference features panel discussions that highlight career pathways and provide valuable networking opportunities with fellow undergraduate students, graduate trainees, and medical physics professionals from academic, clinical, and industry backgrounds. CUMPC is organized by graduate students and trainees, providing the organizing committee with meaningful opportunities to develop leadership skills and expand their professional networks. To learn more about CUMPC, please visit our website at https://cumpc.ca.

title: Stochastic rumor propagation dynamics with topological noise and dual refutation mechanisms
journal: International Journal of Modern Physics C
abstract: Most existing rumor propagation models rely on static network topologies and neglect the combined effects between stochastic topological fluctuations and refutation mechanisms, which constrains the models’ ability to characterize spreading dynamic behaviors. This paper develops a stochastic rumor propagation model that integrates topological noise induced by random edge addition and removal with a dual refutation mechanism. By constructing a system of stochastic differential equations and employing Itô’s lemma and stochastic Lyapunov stability theory, we prove the existence and uniqueness of the global positive solution, the exponential stability, and the sufficient conditions for rumor extinction and persistence of the proposed model, and derive the statistical-average propagation threshold under the homogeneous network setting. Numerical simulation results demonstrate that both the intensity of topological noise and the refutation strength exert significant effects on the density evolution of active rumor spreaders.

title: Radium-223 decreases PD-L1 expression in bone metastases: A study with [89Zr]Zr-atezolizumab PET and immunohistological correlation
journal: European Journal of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging
abstract: Abstract Purpose Most patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) do not benefit from treatment with immune checkpoint inhibitors targeting programmed cell death (ligand) 1 (PD-(L)1). Radiation might improve response to immunotherapy by increasing the immunogenicity of prostate cancer. The objective of this study was to investigate radium-223-mediated changes in the micro- and macroenvironment of mCRPC. Methods In this prospective, multicenter study (ICTRP NL-OMON26890), 28 patients with mCRPC and predominantly bone metastases were treated with radium-223, according to standard-of-care. Primary endpoint was failure-free survival (FFS). Imaging included sequential positron emission tomography (PET) with gallium-68 prostate-specific membrane antigen ( 68 Ga-PSMA) and zirconium-89 atezolizumab ( 89 Zr-atezolizumab) to quantify whole-body expression of PD-L1 in vivo (SUV mean/max ). Paired PET analysis included nine patients. The immune status of patients was characterized in biopsies from bone metastases and in blood using (multiplex) immunohistochemistry (IHC) and flow cytometry, respectively. Sequential biopsy analysis included two patients. Results 89 Zr-atezolizumab uptake in 68 Ga-PSMA positive bone metastases showed high intra- and inter-patient heterogeneity. In the total volume of 68 Ga-PSMA-positive bone lesions, the median SUV mean of 89 Zr-atezolizumab was 2.5 (IQR 0.9–3.4) at baseline and 0.9 (IQR 0.5–2.5) after three cycles of radium-223, which was higher than the physiological uptake in bone marrow at baseline and after treatment with radium-223. After three cycles of radium-223, 89 Zr-atezolizumab uptake decreased in bone metastases, independent of response on 68 Ga-PSMA PET, and the number of lymphocytes in tumor tissue and blood decreased concomitantly. Conclusions Treatment of mCRPC bone metastases with radium-223 results in a significant decrease of in vivo PD-L1-expression on PET imaging and a decrease in immune cells in bone metastases and blood. These findings indicate that treatment with alpha emitting radium-223 alters the immune microenvironment, thereby potentially reducing the efficacy of PD-(L)1 inhibitors.

title: In situ and ex situ conservation of medicinal plants: A critical review of current approaches
journal: Journal of Medicinal Plants for Economic Development
abstract: Background: Medicinal plants are indispensable to global health care, cultural heritage and pharmaceutical innovation, yet their survival is increasingly threatened by habitat destruction, overharvesting and climate change. Aim: This review critically examines both in situ and ex situ conservation strategies, highlighting their principles, applications, limitations and complementarities. Setting: In situ methods preserve evolutionary and ecological dynamics within natural habitats, while ex situ approaches provide genetic safeguarding and research opportunities through seed banks, botanical gardens, tissue culture and cryopreservation. Method: This review integrates peer-reviewed literature, institutional reports, case studies and expert observations from 2000 to 2024. Results: Case studies from Asia and Africa illustrate successful conservation models integrating local knowledge and community participation. However, each method faces significant challenges, including land-use conflict, technical limitations, loss of genetic diversity and weak enforcement. Conclusion: The review argues for integrated conservation frameworks that synergise both approaches and leverage modern tools such as genomic technologies, geographic information system and DNA barcoding. Contribution: It underscores the urgency of policy reform, capacity building, sustainable funding and equitable benefit sharing to ensure the long-term survival and sustainable use of medicinal plant resources.

title: ESTIMATING WEATHER AND CLIMATE IMPACTS WITH PANEL MODELS
abstract: This paper begins with an assumed nonlinear effect of climate on an economic outcome and then derives the resulting short-run and long-run behavior to changes in weather. The short-run annual effects are a function of intertemporal weather deviations and the interaction between weather deviations and the long-run marginal effect of climate. One can identify the underlying nonlinear climate effects with these interaction terms. We illustrate these principles by showing how both weather and climate affect annual GDP per capita in a panel of countries. GDP is generally more sensitive to short-run changes in temperature than long-run changes. A long-run [Formula: see text]C warming has a negligible effect on GDP per capita overall, but it will cause losses in the hottest countries of −1% to −1.5% per ∘ C. Precipitation also has a very small effect on GDP per capita. These estimates just reflect the direct effect of temperature and precipitation on the economy and do not reflect nonmarket damages and damages caused by sea level rise and storms.

title: Work Flexibility and Employee Performance in Hybrid Work Systems: The Mediating Role of Work-Life Balance and Financial Management Behavior
abstract: This study examined the associations among Flexible Work Arrangement (X), Work-Life Balance (M1), Financial Management Behavior (M2), and Employee Performance (Y) among employees using hybrid or flexible work systems. A quantitative, explanatory, cross-sectional survey was conducted with 300 respondents aged 20–45. The questionnaire contained 38 indicators measured on a five-point Likert scale, and the model was estimated using Structural Equation Modeling based on Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) with SmartPLS 4. The reported measurement results met the manuscript's stated thresholds: all outer loadings exceeded 0.70, AVE values exceeded 0.50, and reliability and discriminant-validity indicators were within the reported criteria. Positive direct associations were reported for X→M1 (β = 0.687, p < 0.001), X→M2 (β = 0.247, p < 0.001), X→Y (β = 0.264, p < 0.001), M1→M2 (β = 0.517, p < 0.001), M1→Y (β = 0.176, p = 0.006), and M2→Y (β = 0.347, p < 0.001). The R² values were 0.471 for M1, 0.504 for M2, and 0.479 for Y. The reported indirect associations were significant for X→M1→Y (β = 0.121, p = 0.008), X→M2→Y (β = 0.086, p < 0.001), and X→M1→M2→Y (β = 0.123, p < 0.001). Because the design was cross-sectional and purposive, the findings describe statistical relationships within the sample and should not be interpreted as causal effects.
